title: The Beach Station Where Signal Meets Sand

features.name: reception tower
features.desc-on-touch: the antenna reaches for signal. in certain weather it receives broadcasts from other years; sometimes it broadcasts backwards

features.name: logbook station
features.desc-on-touch: daily entries recording weather, tides, swimmers assisted. some entries describe incidents that could not have happened. all dates correct

features.name: sand accretion field
features.desc-on-touch: dunes that shift by tide. the wind-patterns sand into a shape resembling script. you cannot quite read it before the tide erases it

features.name: equipment shelter
features.desc-on-touch: a prefab hut holding first-aid kits and old radio equipment. the manuals inside reference procedures that do not exist in any hospital

features.name: tide-writing pool
features.desc-on-touch: at low tide, a shallow pool forms. when you wade in, the water holds the imprint of handwriting; not your own, not anyone's you know

reverie.title: REVERIE — the-beach-where-she-taught-the-water-to-remember
narr: you wade knee-deep while she stands on the sand, holding the old
transceiver. the signal is weak here, caught between land and salt.
she says: the water remembers everything broadcast into it. the water
forgets nothing. she turns the dial. for a moment you hear voices
that are not anyone's, singing in a language neither of you knows,
and she smiles, recognizing it as her handwriting becoming sound.

inscription: the beach receives more than swimmers; some broadcasts are cast into the water itself, and the water learns to answer

file.name: LifeguardLog_Dusk_Entries_1987_1988.txt
file.note: daily observations become increasingly surgical in language; rescue procedures described in terminology that predates modern medicine
